Título: An Efficient and Low-Cost FPGAs-Accelerated CNN-Based Edge Intelligent Garbage Classification System on ZYNQ
Autores: Wang W.; Zhu M.
Revista / congreso: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Neural Networks
Resumen: Garbage classification has achieved a high classification accuracy using convolutional neural network (CNN). However, due to the high complexity of CNNs, CPU or GPU-based solutions are too expensive for daily garbage classification. In this paper, we propose an efficient and low-cost field programmable logic gate arrays (FPGAs) accelerated CNN-based intelligent garbage classification system with two ARM+FPGA heterogeneous platforms. In this work, an image preprocessing module is deployed in the programmable logic of xc7z010clg400-1 to perform the real-time preprocessing of a garbage image. A pre-trained 18-layer CNN model is deployed in the programmable logic of xc7z020clg400-1 with the help of hardware computing module reusing to perform the garbage classification in real time. In the processing system of xc7z010clg400-1 and xc7z020clg400-1, a software to implement the scheduling of hardware is designed. According to the experiments, the system achieved a calculation speed of 21.709 times faster than the Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-7700HQ processor (CPU) and the power consumption is 1/17 of the CPU's. Its classification accuracy on the garbage dataset TrashNet is 93%, which is only 0.333% less than the pure software on the CPU. It is a cheaper solution and can also enhance the efficiency of daily garbage classification based on embedded devices. In the future work, the system we proposed will be a promising solution of the large consumption of time, energy and comnuting resource in previous solutions. © 2021 IEEE.

Título: A Dual-Backbone Transfer Learning Method for Waste Image Classification with Embedded ECA Attention
Autores: T. Ma; H. Zhang; M. Zhang
Revista / congreso: 2026 IEEE 6th International Conference on Computer Systems (ICCS)
Resumen: Intelligent garbage classification serves as a critical technology for solid-waste resource recycling and can effectively cut manual sorting costs. To address the drawbacks of existing deep-learning-based garbage classification approaches, including overfitting under small-sample conditions, insufficient recognition robustness in complex real-world scenarios, and excessive model computational overhead, this paper proposes a dual-backbone differentiated transfer learning method embedded with ECA channel attention. Targeted at the structural characteristics of VGG16 and ResNet50, differentiated layer-freezing depths, optimizers, learning-rate scheduling schemes and regularization strategies are designed for targeted transfer of pre-trained knowledge. Meanwhile, the ECA attention module together with Global Average Pooling (GAP) is introduced for feature enhancement and classification-head optimization. Experiments are carried out on TrashNet and Garbage Classification V2 datasets with an 8:1:1 split for training, validation and test sets, and each group of experiments is independently repeated five times. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved VGG16 achieves a test accuracy of 91.94% on TrashNet, 0.32 percentage points higher than the original model. The improved ResNet50 obtains 93.98% test accuracy on Garbage Classification V2, outperforming its original counterpart by 1.39 percentage points. The proposed method achieves competitive classification performance under diverse data distributions and scene complexities, and reaches a favorable trade-off between classification accuracy and computational overhead.

Apart from classifying waste types, this system helps users get guidelines about steps to follow for disposing and information on disposal centers, which was not provided in the existing waste classification systems where there is no user information provided. The proposed solution, through accurate identification and guidance, helps users act in eco-friendly ways and prevent contamination of recyclable waste.

Título: Reliability Evaluation of CAM-Based XAI for Waste Image Classification
Autores: V. A. Septian; P. Harry Gunawan
Revista / congreso: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Mechatronics Systems (AIMS)
Resumen: The adoption of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in waste image classification continues to grow, yet the claim that Class Activation Mapping (CAM)-based methods are faithful is rarely tested systematically, and almost never on the lightweight architectures that real waste-sorting hardware actually runs. This study evaluates the faithfulness of three CAM methods (Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, Score-CAM) on two edge-deployable backbones (MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB0) across two datasets (TrashNet, Garbage Classification), four masking schemes (blackout, blur, mean imputation, local interpolation), and three deletion ratios, using the Confidence Drop (CD) metric tested against two random baselines via a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction, reported with Cohen’s d effect sizes and 95% confidence intervals. At a deletion ratio of 0.20, 24 of 48 configurations reach significance (p < 0.0042), spread across both architectures (EfficientNetB0 14, MobileNetV2 10) rather than confined to one. Two findings carry direct practical weight. First, blackout masking is an active liability, not a neutral choice: the random baseline matches or exceeds nearly every CAM method under blackout, exposing it as a pseudo-evaluator driven by out-of-distribution artifacts rather than saliency quality; we argue it should be abandoned as a default protocol. Second, faithfulness is not a fixed property of a method but of the interaction between method, masking scheme, and the spatial structure of the object class: classes with compact, centrally located evidence (glass, trash) yield substantially larger faithfulness gaps than classes with diffuse evidence (paper, cardboard), a pattern invisible to generic ImageNet-style evaluation protocols. Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM++ are consistently faithful under non-blackout schemes; Score-CAM fails across all 48 configurations. The backbone effect is real but gradual, reported as associative rather than causal, since each architecture is represented by a single trained instance.

Título: A Smart Wearable-Driven Platform for Sustainable Plastic Tracking Using Mobile and Cloud Technologies
Autores: A. M. Kolla; D. M. Patil; S. Geetha
Revista / congreso: 2026 6th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
Resumen: Plastic-consumption awareness tools commonly rely on retrospective self-reporting and do not provide an immediate physical prompt when a user crosses a personal limit. PlasTrack combines an ESP32-based wearable, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) communication, a barcode-enabled Android application, Firestore synchronization, and a 3-D-printed polylactic-acid enclosure. Each scan updates a daily consumption total and triggers a haptic alert when a configured threshold is met or exceeded. For products without usable barcode metadata, an offline feasibility evaluation examined a user-confirmed material-classification fallback on the public TrashNet dataset. The classifier predicts only material class and does not estimate plastic mass; the user must confirm or enter mass before the total is updated. Validation-based selection compared a majority baseline, logistic regression, a 500-tree random forest, and a principal-component-analysis radial-basis-function support-vector machine (PCA-RBF-SVM). The selected 90%-variance PCA-RBF-SVM achieved 79.58% accuracy and 79.28% macro-F1 on an untouched 431-image test set; plastic-class F1 was 78.57%. Previously reported prototype observations indicated short-range BLE operation and sub-300-ms application-to-alert latency, while a continuous battery duration of 5.2 h remained below a full-day target. The results establish an engineering proof of concept and identify the data, power, and user-study requirements for deployment.

Título: Sustainable Smart Waste Sorting Through Reject-Aware IoT and Calibrated Vision: A Measurement-Calibrated Selective Routing Prototype
Autores: Alhalangy, A
Revista / congreso: SUSTAINABILITY
Resumen: Smart waste systems can support sustainable recycling only when sensing, classification, and routing decisions are linked to transparent uncertainty management. This study aims to develop and evaluate a measurement-calibrated, risk-aware selective routing prototype for sustainable smart waste sorting under bench-scale conditions. The proposed prototype integrates an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensing layer, Arduino Nano control, ESP8266 wireless synchronization, calibration-based fill level conversion, median filtering, exponential smoothing, hysteresis, and persistence-driven alert logic with a conveyor-based single-item vision-routing layer. The sorting layer routes items into glass, metal, plastic, trash, or a reject stream using a reject-aware VGG19 classifier with true logit temperature scaling and calibrated confidence gating. A quantitative prototype-level experimental evaluation was conducted using a five class benchmark of 2527 TrashNet images under a stratified 75/10/15 hold-out design, with cardboard and paper serving as outlier-exposure samples for the reject class. The final model achieved 88.13% test accuracy, 88.15% weighted F1, and 96.60% reject class F1. With a final policy tau = 0.70, the system routed 76.09% of routing class test items with 92.66% routed precision, while reject recall reached 98.66% and reject false acceptance was limited to 1.34%. Structured perturbation testing showed that severe visual degradation reduced automatic routing coverage but mostly shifted uncertain cases toward rejection. The contribution of this work is a transparent prototype-level mechanism that links calibrated sensing, calibrated visual confidence, selective rejection, and actuation-aware routing to support recycling stream purity under bounded uncertainty. Future work should validate the approach under multi-bin, multi-object, and field deployment conditions.

Título: Unsupervised Waste Classification By Dual-Encoder Contrastive Learning and Multi-Clustering Voting (DECMCV)
Autores: Huang K.; Song M.; Ba S.; An L.; Liang H.; Deng H.; Liu Y.; Zhang Z.; Zhou C.
Resumen: Waste classification is crucial for improving processing efficiency and reducing environmental pollution. Supervised deep learning methods are commonly used for automated waste classification, but they rely heavily on large labeled datasets, which are costly and inefficient to obtain. Real-world waste data often exhibit category and style biases, such as variations in camera angles, lighting conditions, and types of waste, which can impact the model's performance and generalization ability. Therefore, constructing a bias-free dataset is essential. Manual labeling is not only costly but also inefficient. While self-supervised learning helps address data scarcity, it still depends on some labeled data and generally results in lower accuracy compared to supervised methods. Unsupervised methods show potential in certain cases but typically do not perform as well as supervised models, highlighting the need for an efficient and cost-effective unsupervised approach. This study presents a novel unsupervised method, Dual-Encoder Contrastive Learning with Multi-Clustering Voting (DECMCV). The approach involves using a pre-trained ConvNeXt model for image encoding, leveraging VisionTransformer to generate positive samples, and applying a multi-clustering voting mechanism to address data labeling and domain shift issues. Experimental results demonstrate that DECMCV achieves classification accuracies of 93.78% and 98.29% on the TrashNet and Huawei Cloud datasets, respectively, outperforming or matching supervised models. On a real-world dataset of 4,169 waste images, only 50 labeled samples were needed to accurately label thousands, improving classification accuracy by 29.85% compared to supervised models. This method effectively addresses style differences, enhances model generalization, and contributes to the advancement of automated waste classification.

Título: Recyclable Waste Identification Using CNN Image Recognition and Gaussian Clustering
Autores: Wang Y.; Zhao W.J.; Xu J.; Hong R.
Resumen: Waste recycling is an important way of saving energy and materials in the production process. In general cases recyclable objects are mixed with unrecyclable objects, which raises a need for identification and classification. This paper proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN) model to complete both tasks. The model uses transfer learning from a pretrained Resnet-50 CNN to complete feature extraction. A subsequent fully connected layer for classification was trained on the augmented TrashNet dataset [1]. In the application, sliding-window is used for image segmentation in the pre-classification stage. In the post-classification stage, the labelled sample points are integrated with Gaussian Clustering to locate the object. The resulting model has achieved an overall detection rate of 48.4% in simulation and final classification accuracy of 92.4%.
